page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-16 is a virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at a nominal frequency of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration features 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs. System memory totals 16.0 GB, which establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio corresponding to 2.0 GB per execution thread.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring persistent operational data and operating system installations to rely on remote block volumes. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on the host. Network resource provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external routing and connectivity.

Configured with a lean memory footprint relative to its processing cores, VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-16 emphasizes computational execution over in-memory caching. This allocation profile delivers cost-effective compute capacity for tasks that do not require extensive RAM, making it suitable for distributed build agents, continuous integration runners, batch computing, API services, and stateless web application serving.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.4-16 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The configuration provides 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, allocating 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, reflecting a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying on external block storage for persistent data needs while including one complimentary public IPv4 address for network access. With dedicated CPU allocation and 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance type provides consistent execution capacity without the overhead of surplus memory. It is suited for compute-focused tasks that operate within moderate memory boundaries, such as CI/CD build environments, batch data processing, web application backends, and containerized microservices.
